question: A bicycle workshop keeps all of its spokes in one bin. The bin held 224 spokes, and a repair job put 21 more back into it. The wholesaler then filled the bin to 7 times that number. A customer donated 60 spokes from an old wheel, and a colleague added 73. The workshop is open 5 days a week. The chain now wants 6 workshops with bins holding as many spokes as this one. How many spokes will the 6 workshops need?

A print shop ordered 7 cases of ink cartridges, each case holding 200 cartridges. Over the year 1324 cartridges were used in the machines and 64 were found to be dried out. The shop has 11 printers. The supplier then delivered 3 times as many cartridges as were left. Head office repeated that order 3 times over for the whole group. A customer returned 35 unopened cartridges. How many cartridges does the shop have now?

A juice press keeps all of its bottles in one chilled room. On Monday morning 6 crates were carried in, each holding 223 bottles. Before lunch a farm added 37 bottles to the same room. During the afternoon 1077 bottles were loaded onto vans for the shops. Half of the bottles in the room are apple juice. That evening a cancelled order put 65 bottles back into the chilled room. How many bottles are in the chilled room now?

A museum shop counts its pencils one by one rather than by the box. The tray held 204 pencils, and 181 were sold during the half-term week. A further 4 were snapped by visitors and thrown away. The shop has 7 windows. The buyer then ordered enough pencils for the tray to hold 8 times as many as were left. A school returned 23 pencils it had not needed. How many pencils are in the tray now?

On Monday morning a farm carted in 7 loads of hay, each load holding 223 bales. In the afternoon a neighbour delivered 44 bales and a contractor added 40 more. Half of the bales were stacked at the back of the barn. That evening 265 bales were sold to a stables. Over the winter the cattle ate 1254 bales. How many bales are left in the barn?

Ravi's tea garden picks more leaves than Sunil's does. One basket held 129 handfuls of leaves until 96 were spoiled by rain and thrown out. A picker then added 40 handfuls to the same basket. Each picker fills 8 baskets like that in a day, and there are 7 pickers on the slope. The garden works 2 shifts a day, and the estate has 9 slopes worked in exactly the same way. How many handfuls of leaves does the estate gather in a day?

On Monday morning a garden centre had 65 saplings in the polytunnel, and Marta plants more of them than Kwesi does. Before lunch 50 saplings were sold to a park. In the afternoon the nursery delivered enough for the tunnel to hold 9 times as many saplings as were left. The polytunnel is 18 metres long. That evening Kwesi brought in 10 saplings from his own garden, and on Tuesday a grower added 72 more. How many saplings are in the polytunnel now?

A fish market records its landings in crates rather than in kilograms, and Ola lands more than Bram does. On Tuesday morning each of the 3 boats brought in 15 crates. At midday a second landing doubled the number of crates on the quay. In the afternoon a trawler added 59 crates. That evening Bram brought in 68 more. How many crates are on the quay now?

A council counts its recycling bins one by one rather than by the street. The depot held 202 bins, and a delivery added 72 more. A contractor returned 5 bins and a school sent back 25. During the spring 178 bins were given out to new houses. A neighbouring council then transferred 42 bins to the same depot. How many bins are at the depot now?

A cider brewery keeps all of its bottles in one cellar. The cellar held 109 bottles, and a bottling run added 39 more. The brewery then filled the cellar to 5 times that number for the summer. The bottles were shared equally between the 4 pubs the brewery supplies, and one pub took its share. The brewery was founded in 1902. A cancelled order added 75 bottles to that pub's stock, the chain then ordered 7 times that many for all its houses, and 23 of those were broken in transit. How many bottles arrived safely?

A carpet shop measures its rolls in whole metres rather than in centimetres. A delivery of 167 metres arrived and the supplier then tripled it. A hotel job used 324 metres and a school corridor took another 87. The shop is 20 metres from the station. The chain now wants 9 branches each holding as much carpet as this one. How many metres will the 9 branches hold?

An ambulance station counts its bandages singly rather than by the box, and Ade uses more of them on a shift than Marion does. The store held 98 bandages, and a delivery added 31. A hospital sent 13 more and a charity gave 11. During the winter 88 bandages were used on call-outs. The service now wants 6 stores holding as many bandages as this one, and the region has 3 services set up in exactly the same way. How many bandages will the region hold?

A hotel counts its pillows one by one rather than by the room. On Monday morning the linen store held 91 pillows, and a delivery added 80 before lunch. In the afternoon 84 pillows were taken up to the new rooms. That evening the manager ordered enough for the store to hold 4 times as many pillows as were left. On Tuesday a guest room returned 9 pillows to the store. How many pillows are in the linen store now?

Selina's print room turns out more envelopes than Marc's does. The tray held 195 envelopes, and a machine added 4 more. The works then produced 9 times that many envelopes for the mailing. Marc added 37 envelopes he had addressed by hand. The company now needs 6 mailings of exactly that size. How many envelopes will the 6 mailings need?

A council bought 7 crates of laptops for its schools, each crate holding 106 laptops. The supplier then delivered 3 times that many for the whole borough. The laptops were shared equally between the 6 districts, and one district took its share. The borough has 45 schools. That district's allocation was later increased to 3 times its size by a government grant. A charity then added 69 laptops to the district's total. How many laptops does the district have?

Hector's quarry cuts more stone blocks than Rosa's quarry does. His yard took in 9 wagons, each carrying 166 blocks. A second delivery doubled the number of blocks in the yard. A bridge job then used 1854 blocks and a sea wall took another 917. How many blocks are left in the yard?

Delphine's theatre owns more costumes than Ihsan's does. Her wardrobe was stocked with 5 rails holding 232 costumes each. The costumes were shared equally between the 4 productions of the season, and one production took its share. The theatre seats 400 people. That production returned 224 costumes to the hire company, lost 20 in a flood, and sent 29 away to be repaired. How many costumes does that production still have?

Kaia sets more climbing holds than her colleague Ben does. The store held 177 holds, and 127 of them were bolted onto the new wall. A supplier then delivered 53 holds to the same store. A sponsor doubled the number of holds in the store. Ben added 8 holds he had been keeping in his van. How many holds are in the store now?

A market garden records its crop in single cucumbers rather than in kilograms. On Monday morning each of the 3 rows was picked and gave 34 cucumbers. By the afternoon 5 greenhouses had been picked in exactly the same way. That evening a second picking doubled the day's total. The site has 12 water tanks. The cucumbers were then shared equally between the 4 shops the site supplies. How many cucumbers did one shop receive?

A pet shop had 71 sacks of bird seed in the store, and 35 were sold in the first week of winter. A supplier returned 17 sacks that had been ordered by mistake. The shop then took in 8 times as many sacks as it was holding, ready for the cold snap. The shop stays open until 6 o'clock, and half of the sacks are kept in the back room. A wholesaler finally delivered 75 more sacks. How many sacks of bird seed does the shop have now?

Ferdi's hardware shop sells more paintbrushes than Anya's shop does. His store took in 7 boxes, each holding 133 brushes. A rep left 45 sample brushes at the shop. A decorating firm bought 354 brushes and a college took another 313. Anya then sent over 58 brushes she could not sell. The chain now wants 6 shops each holding as many brushes as Ferdi's. How many brushes will the 6 shops hold?

The Fenwick lighting depot received a shipment of 124 pallets. Each pallet was stacked with 8 crates, and every crate held 3 desk lamps. After the shipment was counted, the supplier sent over 18 extra lamps to replace damaged ones. Later that week a hotel returned 56 lamps it had never unpacked, and these went onto the same shelves. The depot manager, who has run the floor for a dozen years, wants a fresh count. How many desk lamps does the depot hold now?

Ms. Alvarez started Saturday with 142 concert tickets in her folder. During the morning she handed 39 of them to the school choir for free. In the afternoon she returned 57 unsold tickets to the box office window. Every ticket she still had left was sold during the evening for 7 dollars each, and although her old ledger records amounts in cents she rewrote the takings in dollars. A patron who had bought a dozen programmes then added 73 dollars to her takings as a tip. How many dollars did Ms. Alvarez have at the end of the evening?

A collector poured 212 glass marbles into 4 identical tins, dividing them equally so that each tin held the same number. Into one of those tins she dropped 70 more marbles she had found under the workbench, a bench that has stood in her shed for a dozen winters. Her nephew then borrowed 55 marbles from that same tin for a game in the garden. She afterwards filled 8 tins so that every one of them matched that tin exactly, marble for marble. The corner shop sells these marbles in bags of 39, and she prefers to weigh her collection in grams rather than kilograms. How many marbles are in those 8 matching tins altogether?

A furniture workshop opened a carton holding 27 boxes of screws. Each box contained 6 packets, and every packet held 7 small cards. Each card carried 3 screws pressed into the backing. Over a busy month the workshop drove 2657 of these screws into flat-pack wardrobes. The foreman has been assembling wardrobes for a dozen different shops. How many screws from that carton are still unused?
